version.value: Original scoring for violin, cello and piano
version.note: The original label identifies the movement and the three instruments. The session’s edition and part materials are not established. Section timings follow the score and the recording’s broad contrasts; there is no bar-level alignment or listening review.

performers.note: The label names The Mannes-Gimpel-Silva Trio and prints Gimpel’s given name as Bronislav; that spelling is retained.

date.note: Jonathan Woolf identifies Clara’s Trio as recorded at the same 1951 sessions as the Beethoven coupling. No precise session date is established. The Archive date field separately describes the LP publication.

place.note: The transfer metadata and consulted reissue review do not establish the recording venue. The US release country is not treated as a session location.

label.note: Original 33⅓-rpm LP label, not the Forgotten Records reissue.

catalogue.note: Internet Archive dates the LP to 1951. A contemporary review independently establishes commercial publication by September 1952; the rights assessment uses that documented upper bound.

matrixTakeSides.value: Side 1, band 3; printed label matrix MG 2301
matrixTakeSides.note: The Andante is the third movement listed on side 1 and the third segmented derivative. MG 2301 is the printed side matrix. No individual take or tape number is established.

credits.note: The item belongs to the Boston Public Library vinyl collection. No unverified personal mastering credit is inferred from operator accounts.

date.note: The ripping_date field is 20210715042255. This is the transfer date; the sleeve and labels were scanned separately in June 2021.

processing.value: Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; segmented VBR MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: The playback and digitisation chain is stated in the item’s lineage field. Equalisation, pitch correction and noise-reduction settings are not documented.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a mono vinyl LP transfer

composition.value: Public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms; the original score was published in 1847 and Clara Schumann died in 1896.
composition.note: This assessment concerns the historical composition and first edition, not an unidentified modern edition or every jurisdiction.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis: commercial publication on Decca DL 9555 documented by September 1952, before 1963.
recording.note: The project’s pre-1963 rule relies on expiry of the former 50-year phonogram term before the 2013 extension. Audio Engineering reviews this LP in September 1952. The year 1952 is a conservative publication-by date, distinct from the documented 1951 sessions and the Archive’s 1951 release attribution. US recording status is not established. rights.creditLine: Clara Schumann, Piano Trio in G minor, Op. 17: III. Andante; The Mannes-Gimpel-Silva Trio — Leopold Mannes, piano; Bronislav Gimpel, violin; Luigi Silva, cello. Recorded 1951; Decca DL 9555, published by September 1952; Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US recording status not established.

sources.locator: Printed p. 48 (PDF p. 50), under “Some novel Romantics”: Clara Schumann, Trio in G minor, Op. 17; Beethoven, Trio No. 8 in B flat; Mannes-Gimpel-Silva Trio; Decca DL 9555. A contemporary commercial-release review, establishing publication before 1963.

sources.title: Clara Schumann — Piano Trio, first edition, Breitkopf & Härtel, plate 7562
sources.locator: Sibley Music Library scan, printed pp. 20–23 inspected visually: piano alone, violin with pizzicato cello, cello continuation, più animato at bar 25, Tempo I and cello melody at bar 53, final G-major cadence.

sources.title: IMSLP — Piano Trio in G minor, Op. 17
sources.locator: Composition 1846; first edition, plate 7562, dated 1847 by Hofmeister reference; four movements and original instrumentation.

sources.title: Los Angeles Philharmonic — Clara Schumann, Piano Trio
sources.locator: Andante characterised as an instrumental song in G major with an E-minor contrasting middle section.

sources.title: Robert Greenberg — Robert and Clara Schumann Complete Piano Trios, National Recording Registry essay
sources.locator: Pp. 3–4: Clara’s dates, composition of the Trio between May and September 1846, first chamber composition, and previous study and performance of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven. The essay concerns the later Beaux Arts recording, not this Decca session.
